title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff ordering and regional failover under load
author: Aisha Khan
description: Context: In production during a regional capacity event we observed SLO enforcer thrashing where multiple regions repeatedly triggered regional failover and circuit-breaker backoff ordering regressions. This caused unnecessary load-shedding and prolonged service degradation for a subset of customers. Root cause: a race in slo-enforcer's backoff scheduling combined with non-deterministic region ordering allowed stale backoff entries to re-open prematurely, and the regional failover path would then re-route requests in a pattern that repeatedly tripped our cluster-level circuit breakers. This PR is a hotfix to harden ordering, tighten thresholds, and add safe guards so failovers do not trigger oscillation. What this PR changes: 1) Enforce monotonic backoff sequence numbers and use compare-and-swap when updating region backoff state to prevent stale writes. 2) Introduce a per-customer-region failover mutex to serialize failover decisions for the same customer across regions. 3) Tighten backoff decay thresholds and add jitter to avoid synchronized reopen across regions. 4) Add new fallback routing policy: when a region is under backoff, route to next healthy region but mark requests as prefetched so KV cache warming is delayed to avoid transient cache pressure. 5) Observability: new metrics (slo_enforcer.backoff_rejects, slo_enforcer.failover_serialization_wait_ms) and a dashboard update, plus event logs for backoff-update failures. 6) Add integration tests and a perf-canary scenario that replays the incident traffic pattern. Rollout plan: merge to main, then immediate canary rollout to prod regions us-west1, eu-central1 with 10% traffic for 30 minutes, monitor SLOs and slo_enforcer.backoff_rejects. If stable, promote to 50% then full. Rollback: revert the feature flag (slo_enforcer.backoff_serialization) or immediately rollback the deploy; the change is guarded by a feature flag for quick rollback. Testing: unit tests for CAS logic, deterministic concurrency tests, integration test that simulates region outage and verifies no oscillation, and perf canary against recorded workload. Risks and mitigations: small risk of increased tail latency during failover serialization; mitigated by keeping serialization window small and adding metrics to detect stalls. Related work: ENG-4312 (stability), SRE-187 (regional failover postmortem).
commits: ca9b2d9: enforce CAS updates for backoff state and add monotonic sequence checks
f1e3a7b: add per-customer-region failover mutex and serialize decision path
b7c4f11: tuning thresholds, add jitter, add metrics and integration test scenario
review_comments: Mateo Ruiz: Can you explain why CAS is sufficient here vs an explicit distributed lock? I'm worried about edge cases where multiple regions race on the same sequence number.

Aisha Khan: CAS is sufficient for the backoff state since we include a monotonically increasing sequence number derived from the event timestamp + instance id. For multi-region races the per-customer-region mutex serializes higher-level decisions so CAS only needs to protect the state update itself.
Jing Wei: Integration test looks good; saw a flake on first CI run due to test harness timing, suggest adding a 200ms buffer in the harness.
Aisha Khan: Added the 200ms buffer and re-ran; CI passed on second run.
release_notes: Hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer regional failover and backoff ordering to prevent oscillation and unnecessary load-shedding. Adds safe guards, metrics, and a per-region serialization path. Rollout guarded by feature flag.
